name: t'way livery
description: White fuselage with a red crown band running forward from the red fin and tapering out over the wing. A big white lower-case 't' with a green apostrophe on the fin; 't'way' huge in red lower case across the forward windows, its apostrophe green; red winglets; 'www.twayair.com' in red on the white engines.

areas.name: red crown band from the fin, tapering forward

logos.description: The t'way symbol: a big white lower-case 't' (stem, crossbar, the foot turning right as read) with a green leaf-like apostrophe at its upper right; it reads the same way on both sides.
A small Taegukgi ahead of the registration above the rear windows.

titles.style: The t'way wordmark, huge across the forward windows from just aft of door 1: heavy rounded sans in lower case, the 't' tall, the apostrophe a green leaf, the 'y' descending.
The web address in small bold red lower case along the outboard cowl.

notes: Drawn from A330-300 HL8560 (2026-06-04, right), 737-800 HL8324 (2024-11-20, left from below) and 737-800 HL8235 (2026-02-15). The winglets carry 't way' small in white. The title's 'height' is the raised 't' (its top to the baseline of 'way'). T'way Air became Trinity Airways on 2026-09-10 (same TW/TWB codes) and a gray and rose-gold livery began on 737-8 HL8754 (see trinity-2026); with no openly licensed photo of it yet, this t'way scheme, still on almost the whole fleet, stays the drawn standard here until the new one can be drawn. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on HL8235 (737-800, the commonest type): the wordmark's 'way' stands 0.78 of the height from the raised 't's top to the baseline (type.xHeight); the crown band's lower edge is a curve, now drawn smooth.
history: Replaced Skyarium v1's approximation. The scheme since t'way's 2010 launch; being replaced by the Trinity Airways livery from September 2026.
